summary: Jules Mohl was an Iranian, Central Asian, and Sinology scholar. He studied at the University of Tübingen (~1818–1823) and under Silvestre de Sacy and Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat (~1823–1826). He held posts at Tübingen (1826) and the Collège de France (1847–1876).

Jules Oppert worked in Indology, history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at the Gelehrtenschule des Johanneums, Heidelberg (~1844), Bonn (~1844–1845), Humboldt University (~1845–1846), and Kiel (~1846–1847). He served as professor at the Collège de France (1874–1905).

Julia Ching was a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and philosophy. She studied at the College of New Rochelle (~1954–1958), Catholic University of America, and Australian National University (~1969–1971), and was later based at the University of Toronto (~1978–2001).

Julia F. Andrews specializes in Sinology, history, and archaeology. She studied at Brown University (~1969–1973), UC Berkeley, and Harvard University (~1977–1984). She held an academic post at Ohio State University (~1987).
Julia Leslie was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. She founded and held a post at SOAS University of London (~1993–2004).

Julian Strube specializes in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Heidelberg University (2005–2015, 2020) and Amsterdam (2009–2010). He held posts at Heidelberg (2015–2019), Amsterdam (2016–2017), Münster (2019–2021), and Vienna (~2021).

Juliane Schober works in religious and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in 1989 and served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Arizona State University (attested 2007).
Julie A. Gifford is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Chicago under Frank E. Reynolds and held a post at Miami University.

Julius Eggeling was an Indologist who studied under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler at Breslau (~1862–1865) and Albrecht Weber at Humboldt University Berlin (~1865–1867). He served at University College London (1872–1875) and the University of Edinburgh (~1875–1914).

Julius Euting specialized in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at Maulbronn and Blaubeuren seminaries and at Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth (~1857–1861). He held positions at the University of Strasbourg and its library (~1872–1909).

Julius Grill was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tübingen (~1858–1862) under Rudolf von Roth and Adalbert Kuhn. He held professorships at the Maulbronn and Blaubeuren seminaries (~1875–1898) and Tübingen (1888).

Julius Jolly was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Albrecht Weber at Humboldt University Berlin (~1869–1871) and Martin Haug (~1871–1872). He served as professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology at the University of Würzburg (~1877–1923).

Julius Lipner specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at King's College London, Clare Hall, Cambridge, and Birmingham (~1971–1974). He held posts at the University of Birmingham (~1973–1975) and the University of Cambridge (~1975).
Jun Fujii is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctoral degree from the University of Tokyo. He held a lecturing post at Komazawa University (~2011–2014).

Jun Takashima specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied under Minoru Hara at the University of Tokyo (~1974–1980) and at Kyoto University (~1980–1985). He held posts at Aichi Prefectural University (~1990–1994) and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~2001–2021).

Jundo Nagashima specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Taisho University under Seitatsu Matsunami, under Alexis Sanderson, and under Paul Williams at the University of Bristol (attested 2002). He served as a lecturer at Taisho University (attested 2006–2017).

June McDaniel is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She studied at Emory University and the University of Chicago, and held professorial posts in religious studies and philosophy at the College of Charleston (attested 2000, 2015).

Junglan Bang works in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Seung-suk Jung and Sungdoo Ahn at Dongguk University, and under Harunaga Isaacson at the University of Hamburg (PhD 2012). She served as a visiting researcher at Kyoto University.

Jungmin Ha works in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. She completed an MA under Juhyung Rhi at Seoul National University and a PhD under Stanley Abe at Duke University (attested 2016).

Junjirō Takakusu was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Friedrich Max Müller, Moriz Winternitz, and Sylvain Lévi. He held posts at Tokyo Imperial University (1897–1927), Osaka University of Foreign Studies (~1921–1923), and Musashino Junior College (~1924–1944).
